neighbours.label: ' whole' / ' entire' stressing the surprising scale of something ('an entire city of the dead', 'a whole line of')
fire: It wasn't one small tomb, but an entire town beneath the sand.
Had she stumbled on a whole family of new drugs?
It soon turned out there was a whole network of tunnels.
They found not one ship but an entire fleet on the seabed.
He had invented a whole new class of materials.
Behind the wall lay an entire library of old books.
There is a whole world of insects under this log.
The storm wiped out an entire village in one night.
quiet: It wasn't one small tomb, but two old jars beneath the sand.
Had she stumbled on a bottle of old drugs?
It soon turned out there was a loose brick in the tunnel.
They found not one ship but a small boat on the seabed.
He had bought a new pair of boots.
Behind the wall lay a shelf of old books.
There is a small beetle under this log.
The storm knocked out a street light in one night.
